questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about PM Vishwakarma Scheme (2023):
1. It provides support to traditional artisans and craftspeople
2. It covers 18 trades including blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, carpenters
3. Benefits include skill training, toolkit, credit support up to ₹3 lakh
4. It is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% Central funding
questions.explanation: All correct. PM Vishwakarma (Sept 2023, ₹13,000 crore for 5 years): targets traditional artisans working with hands/tools across 18 trades (carpenter, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, sculptor, cobbler, tailor, washer, basket/mat weaver, doll-maker, barber, garland-maker, boat-maker, armourer, locksmith, hammer & toolkit maker, fishing net maker). Benefits: recognition (PM Vishwakarma certificate+ID), skill training (basic+advanced), toolkit incentive (₹15,000), credit (₹1 lakh → ₹2 lakh at 5% interest), marketing support, digital transactions incentive.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to PM-JANMAN (Janjatiya Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan):
1. It targets Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
2. India has 75 PVTGs across 18 states and UTs
3. It aims to provide basic facilities: housing, roads, water, electricity, health
4. PVTGs are identified by pre-agricultural technology level and declining population
questions.explanation: All correct. PM-JANMAN (Nov 2023, ₹24,000 crore): saturate PVTG habitations with basic infrastructure. 75 PVTGs (identified by Dhebar Commission criteria: pre-agricultural economy, declining/stagnant population, low literacy, subsistence economy). Spread across 18 states/UTs in ~22,000 villages. Components: Pradhan Mantri PVTG Development Mission (PMPDM) integrating 11 interventions: PMAY houses, road connectivity, Jal Jeevan, electricity, mobile towers, Anganwadis, schools, health facilities, nutrition, livelihood.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana:
1. It provides free electricity up to 300 units/month through rooftop solar
2. Target: 1 crore households to get rooftop solar systems
3. Central financial assistance provided for installation
4. Net metering allows selling excess solar power back to the grid
questions.explanation: All correct. PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024, ₹75,021 crore): rooftop solar for residential households. 300 units free/month (through solar generation — not from grid for free). Target: 1 crore homes. CFA: ₹30,000/kW for first 2 kW + ₹18,000/kW for additional (up to 3 kW). Net metering: excess generation fed to grid, credited in bill. Apply via national portal. Subsidized bank loans arranged. Links to India's 500 GW non-fossil target. Reduces electricity bills to near-zero for small households.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to Lakhpati Didi scheme:
1. It aims to create 3 crore 'Lakhpati Didis' (women earning ₹1 lakh+/year)
2. It works through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) under DAY-NRLM
3. It focuses on skill development, micro-enterprise, and market linkage
4. It was announced in Independence Day speech 2023 and expanded in Budget 2024
questions.explanation: All correct. Lakhpati Didi: target initially 2 crore (Aug 2023) → expanded to 3 crore (Budget 2024-25). Through SHG ecosystem under DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission). Already 1 crore+ women achieved Lakhpati status. Mechanism: skilling in locally relevant trades (food processing, handloom, livestock, organic farming), micro-enterprise development, market access, digital literacy. 10 crore women in 90 lakh+ SHGs form the base. Builds on SHG-Bank Linkage (largest microfinance globally).

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation):
1. It targets universal water supply in all 4,700+ statutory towns
2. It aims to make cities 'water secure' through recycling and reuse
3. It promotes rejuvenation of water bodies and wetlands in urban areas
4. AMRUT 1.0 was limited to only 500 cities
questions.explanation: All correct. AMRUT 2.0 (Oct 2021, ₹2.87 lakh crore): massive expansion from AMRUT 1.0 (2015, 500 cities only). Components: universal water supply coverage (100% households), 100% sewerage/septage management in 500 cities, rejuvenation of water bodies, water recycling/reuse. Pey Jal Survekshan (water supply ranking of cities). Technologies promoted: decentralized waste water treatment, SCADA monitoring, reducing non-revenue water (<20%). Target: make Indian cities water-secure and reduce groundwater exploitation.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP):
1. It develops border villages to counter China's Xiaokang village strategy
2. It covers villages in Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Ladakh
3. It provides: road connectivity, housing, tourism promotion, livelihood support
4. First phase covers 2,500+ villages along the northern border
questions.explanation: All correct. VVP (Budget 2022-23): responds to China's Xiaokang model villages along LAC. Target: 2,963 villages in 46 blocks across 19 districts in 5 states/UTs bordering China. Components: road/telecom connectivity, PMAY houses, solar power, tourism circuits (home stays, adventure tourism), livelihood diversification, DTH/OTT services. Phase 1: 663 villages. Strategic objective: retain population in border areas (counter depopulation), create 'eyes and ears' along the border, demonstrate governance presence vs China's infrastructure aggression.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about National Green Hydrogen Mission:
1. India targets 5 MMT annual green hydrogen production by 2030
2. SIGHT programme provides incentives for electrolyser manufacturing
3. Total outlay is ₹19,744 crore
4. Green hydrogen can replace coking coal in steel production
questions.explanation: All correct. National Green Hydrogen Mission (Jan 2023): 5 MMT/year by 2030 (export hub ambition). SIGHT (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition): ₹17,490 crore for electrolyser manufacturing incentive + green hydrogen production incentive. Total mission: ₹19,744 crore. Applications: steel (direct reduced iron using H2 instead of coal), refineries (replacing grey hydrogen), transport (fuel cells), ammonia (green fertilizers), city gas. Expected: 125 GW renewable energy demand, 50 lakh jobs, ₹8 lakh crore investment, 50 MMT CO2 reduction by 2030.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to PM-eBus Sewa scheme:
1. It supports deployment of 10,000 electric buses in cities
2. It operates on a PPP model with government providing Viability Gap Funding
3. It aims to reduce urban transport emissions and improve air quality
4. It covers only metro cities with population above 50 lakh
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — PM-eBus Sewa is NOT limited to metro/50 lakh+ cities. It covers cities with 3 lakh+ population (169 cities). Two segments: Segment 1 (10,000 e-buses in PPP mode for cities without organized bus service), Segment 2 (Green Urban Mobility Initiatives — bus priority lanes, NCMC-based ticketing). ₹57,613 crore outlay. Buses procured by private operators, cities pay per-km service charge, VGF from Centre. Links to India's EV ecosystem push and NCAP air quality targets.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
Consider the following about SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas):
1. It provides 'Record of Rights' to rural homeowners using drone surveys
2. Property cards issued are called 'Gharauni/Property Cards'
3. It enables rural residents to use property as collateral for bank loans
4. It has been implemented only in 5 pilot states
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — SVAMITVA was initially piloted in 6 states (2020) but has been EXPANDED to all states/UTs (full rollout from 2021). Uses: Survey of India drones for precise boundary mapping of 'abadi' (inhabited) areas in villages. Property cards enable: bank loans using land as collateral (previously impossible without formal title), reduction in property disputes, better rural planning. 1.5+ crore property cards distributed. Panchayats get better property tax base. Beneficiaries: rural homeowners who never had formal ownership documents.

questions.subject: Government Schemes
questions.question:
With reference to Agnipath/Agniveer scheme:
1. Youth are recruited for a 4-year tenure in Armed Forces
2. 25% are retained for further 15-year regular service
3. Seva Nidhi package (~₹11.71 lakh) provided upon exit after 4 years
4. Agniveers get the same pension and gratuity benefits as regular soldiers
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Agniveers (the 75% who exit after 4 years) do NOT get pension or gratuity. They get Seva Nidhi (their contribution + government contribution + interest = ~₹11.71 lakh lump sum) and are prioritized for: CAPF/state police recruitment, higher education (skill certificates), bank loans for entrepreneurship. Only the 25% retained as regulars get pension/gratuity after 15 years. This lack of pension is a major criticism — argument: 4 years too short for pension; counter-argument: young soldiers need post-service support.
